title: Checkout Service Roadmap
eyebrow: Storefront · from the monolith to a checkout service
subtitle: Checkout runs as its own service behind the storefront, with the old code path deleted.

goal.title: End state
goal.what: Checkout is served by its own service, publishes order events, and the monolith keeps no checkout code.

steps.label: Groundwork
steps.title: Checkout module boundary
steps.what: Checkout code calls the rest of the monolith only through one interface.
steps.why: The service can only be cut out along a boundary that already exists.

steps.label: Groundwork
steps.title: Move cart pricing
steps.what: Cart pricing moves behind the checkout interface.
steps.why: Pricing is the largest dependency checkout has on the monolith.

steps.label: Decision
steps.title: Tax stays in the monolith
steps.what: Checkout asks the monolith for tax instead of owning it.
steps.why: Tax rules change with finance's release cycle, not checkout's.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.title: Checkout service package
steps.what: A new service with the cart and order APIs, deployed but not yet taking traffic.
steps.why: Everything after this routes traffic to it.

related.label: Follow-up: retry budget for the order API

steps.label: Step 4
steps.title: Move payment calls
steps.what: The payment provider is called from the service, not the monolith.
steps.why: Payments are the last thing tying checkout to the monolith.

steps.label: Step 5
steps.title: Delete the old checkout path
steps.what: Remove the monolith's checkout controllers and jobs.
steps.why: Two live paths drift; deleting one is the point of the project.

steps.label: Groundwork
steps.title: Order events schema
steps.what: One versioned schema for order created, paid and refunded.
steps.why: Consumers need a contract before anything publishes.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.title: Publish order events
steps.what: The order API publishes an event for every state change.
steps.why: Fulfillment and email stop reading the checkout tables.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.title: Event replay tool
steps.what: Replay a time range of order events to one consumer.
steps.why: A consumer that missed events can catch up without a database copy.

steps.label: Prep
steps.title: Load test plan
steps.what: Peak-day traffic profile and pass criteria for the service.
steps.why: Cutover needs a number to beat.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.title: Shadow traffic
steps.what: Mirror live checkout requests to the service and compare results.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.title: Cut over
steps.what: Route checkout to the service behind a percentage flag.
steps.why: The flag makes rollback one setting.
